blind_spots.blind_spot: The marketing repeatedly promises 'operator-controlled' field updates but never addresses who trains that operator, what happens on unit rotation, or how tuning knowledge transfers when the trained soldier PCSs out.
blind_spots.operator_reality: A field-level model-tuning capability is only as durable as the training pipeline behind it; without a named train-the-trainer program, the capability degrades to whatever the last operator happened to learn informally.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The company's public materials are written from the product-capability side (what the software can do), not the sustainment/handoff side (who keeps it working after fielding).
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Field-Level Updates: Operators tune and update models at the point of use.

blind_spots.blind_spot: Despite marketing fluency in DDIL/edge deployment language, the actual product documentation for the two questions that matter most operationally — 'How are SensorOps systems deployed?' and 'Can SensorOps integrate with existing systems?' — is unwritten lorem-ipsum placeholder text on the live site.
blind_spots.operator_reality: This is a documentation/integration-engineering debt hiding behind strong deployment marketing copy: an evaluator (or a prime doing integration diligence) who clicks past the homepage into product-information finds the exact deployment-mechanics answers missing.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: A ~13-18 person team building three product lines at once (TargetModeler, SynDOJO, TacOS) plausibly ran out of bandwidth to finish integration-specific documentation even while the marketing narrative got polished.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: How are SensorOps systems deployed ? Far far away, behind the word mountains, far from the countries Vokalia and Consonantia, there live the blind texts.

blind_spots.blind_spot: The company markets simultaneously into DoD components, CBP/border security, law enforcement/EMS/SWAT, and critical infrastructure/industrial operators — four different compliance regimes (DoD ATO/RMF, CJIS for law enforcement, industrial/OT security) — and never names any of them by their specific framework.
blind_spots.operator_reality: A small team spreading across defense, public-safety, and industrial verticals at once risks under-resourcing the specific compliance path (ATO for DoD networks vs. CJIS for police data vs. OT security for pipelines) that any one buyer actually requires before procurement can close.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Multi-vertical go-to-market is a growth strategy for a small, well-funded team; compliance-framework-specific engineering typically lags the sales narrative.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Serving: Department of Defense (DoD) components, U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), intelligence and surveillance units, and maritime and border security teams.

opener_hook: Your product-information page's 'How are SensorOps systems deployed?' answer is still lorem-ipsum placeholder text — an odd gap for a platform whose whole pitch is solving deployment.
what_they_do: AI platform for autonomous systems (TargetModeler for synthetic training data, SynDOJO for simulation/rehearsal, TacOS for edge deployment) built explicitly for offline, low-bandwidth, GPS-denied defense and public-safety environments.
